grand_strategy.reading:
Israel in October 2026 runs the strategy of a state that has won every
battle it chose since 7 October 2023 and cannot convert any of them into an end
state. Its method is preventive, decapitating force within a patron's shadow:
the Twelve-Day War, the killing of Nasrallah, the Doha strike and the war on
Iran from 28 February 2026 weakened Iran and its allies as an organised threat, and the
buffer zones in Gaza (about 60%), Lebanon (about 65 villages) and Syria (nine
posts) are meant to make that victory permanent. Luttwak's paradox is that each
instrument of success spoils its sequel: the decapitations leave movements with a
motive and no ceiling, the buffer zones prevent the stabilisation force, the
Lebanon-for-disarmament framework and the Syria talks that would let the army
leave, and the settlement drive moves toward the annexation red lines of the
Emirates, Jordan and Egypt and so away from the Saudi normalisation that would
end the isolation. The relation that governs all the others is the American one:
Israel needs Washington for interceptors and for the deal with
Iran, which Washington signed in June without Israel's consent, and it is
therefore trying to move from aid to 'reciprocal partnership' before the MOU
expires in 2028 while the American public drifts away. In Europe the two logics
meet: Israel sells the continent weapons at record levels (EUR 3bn from Greece
alone) while governments sanction the settlements, and the friendly bloc (Czechia,
Slovakia, Slovenia, Austria) shields it only as long as it keeps winning
elections. Two signals that are not rows: the election of 27 October, in which
the main contenders for prime minister reject a Palestinian state, so that the policy survives a
change of prime minister, and the Lebanon talks, in which the state of Lebanon
signed a document that Hezbollah, the party that actually holds the weapons,
rejects. Israel's real question for 2027 is whether any of its partners will
carry the burden of the 'day after' that it declines to carry itself.
